samples.summary: `config.server` is the one URL component the new hardening leaves completely unvalidated, so it can still retarget the credentialed request (and can leak credentials embedded in it via the dry-run printer)
samples.evidence: `origin()` only strips a single trailing slash: `config.server.replace(/\/$/, '')`. The change's own stated threat model is that argv / `WAFFLEBASE_*` env / a YAML profile are caller-controlled and untrusted (that is exactly why `seg()` now guards `config.workspace`). Under that same model `server` — resolved from `--server`, `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, or `profiles.<name>.server` in `config.ts:90-158` — is equally untrusted and is concatenated raw. Vector: a profile/env value of `https://api.example.com/#` makes every built URL `https://api.example.com/#/api/v1/workspaces/ws/documents/x`; the WHATWG parser treats everything after `#` as a fragment, so `fetch` sends `GET /` to that host with the `Authorization: Bearer <api key>` header attached (`http-client.ts:140`) — the same 'request goes somewhere other than the path named' outcome the diff fixes for path segments. A value of `https://attacker.test` simply exfiltrates the bearer token. Secondarily, a server value carrying userinfo (`https://user:token@host`) is now printed verbatim to stdout by `printDryRunUrl` (`dry-run.ts:31`) for every previewed command. Suggested hardening: parse `config.server` with `new URL()`, require an http/https scheme, and reject a non-empty query, fragment, or userinfo component.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/config/config.ts for any validation of `server` — none in resolveConfig or loadProfile
read packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts to confirm the raw server string is printed

samples.summary: `seg()` escapes arbitrary identifiers rather than validating their shape, so its safety depends on no proxy or server layer decoding the path before routing
samples.evidence: `seg()` accepts any string and relies solely on `encodeURIComponent` plus a bare-dot-segment refusal, so `../../admin/users` is transmitted as `..%2F..%2Fadmin%2Fusers` (asserted in `test/http-client-paths.test.ts`). That is correct for the WHATWG parser in `fetch`, but the escaped traversal survives on the wire: any intermediary that decodes `%2F`/`%2E` before path matching (nginx `proxy_pass` with a URI part, some ingress/normalising WAFs) or a backend that percent-decodes a route param twice re-materialises the `../..` and lands the credentialed request outside the workspace prefix. Document/tab/api-key ids in this system are UUID/slug-shaped (`VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN` exists for file ids in `packages/backend/src/file/file.constants.ts`), so validating against an allowlist pattern and rejecting anything else would remove the dependency on downstream normalisation behaviour instead of merely encoding around it. Reported as hardening: I could not demonstrate a decoding intermediary in this repo's deployment config.

samples.summary: The new `seg()` guard is applied at each call site rather than at the `request()`/`send()` chokepoint, so the public `request(method, path)` remains an unguarded entry point for building an arbitrary path
samples.evidence: `HttpClient.request` is a public method that takes a raw `path` and concatenates it onto `this.base` (`http-client.ts:169-181`), and `send()` (line 136) takes a fully-formed URL. Every current caller happens to interpolate through `seg()`, so there is no live bypass today — I enumerated them: all `this.request(...)` sites are internal to `http-client.ts` (lines 199-381) and all use `seg()`, and no file outside `packages/cli/src/client` calls `.request(` at all. But the property the change advertises ('every identifier interpolated into a request path goes through seg()') is enforced only by convention and comments; nothing in the type system or lint prevents the next `this.request('GET', `/documents/${id}`)` from re-opening the hole, and the guard reads as covered. Enforcing it where the URL is finally assembled (e.g. splitting `path` into segments in `request()`, or a `path` template-tag type that only `seg()` can produce) would make it non-bypassable.
searchedFor: grep `\.request\(|client\.request` across packages/cli — only http-client.ts internal call sites
grep `/documents/|/workspaces/|/api/v1` across packages/cli/src — all interpolations use seg()
grep `fetch\(` across packages/cli/src — login.ts and refreshSession build URLs without ids

samples.summary: The CLI OAuth loopback callback has no `state`/CSRF binding, so any local process or visited web page can inject an attacker's authorization code and silently log the CLI into the attacker's account (pre-existing, out of diff)
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` (login.ts:168-182) resolves on the first `GET /callback?code=<anything>` it receives from 127.0.0.1, with no `state` parameter generated, no `state` echoed in the OAuth URL built at line 36 (`?mode=cli&port=${port}`), no Origin/Sec-Fetch check, and no binding between the code and this CLI invocation. The code is then exchanged at line 56 and the resulting tokens persisted with `saveSession` (line 138). Vector: while `wafflebase login` is waiting (30s window, line 237), a page the user is browsing — or any unprivileged local process — issues `fetch`/`img src` to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<attacker's code>` for candidate ports; the CLI exchanges the attacker's code and writes the attacker's `accessToken`/`refreshToken` and `activeWorkspace` into `~/.wafflebase/session.json`. Every subsequent `docs import` / `files upload` then writes the victim's data into the attacker's workspace. This is classic OAuth login-CSRF / session fixation. Out of the diff, but in the CLI auth path the diff's design doc explicitly discusses (`docs/design/cli.md`: 'The one command the flag does not hold back is `login`'). Fix: generate a random `state`, pass it in the OAuth URL, and reject a callback whose `state` does not match.
searchedFor: grep for `state` / PKCE / `code_verifier` in packages/cli/src — none present
checked the OAuth URL construction at login.ts:36 for a state parameter

verdict.reason: Verified directly: the CLI loopback callback accepts any `GET /callback?code=...` with no state, no per-invocation secret, and no Origin/Sec-Fetch check (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:168-182, 223-226), and the OAuth URL it opens carries no state the CLI could later verify (login.ts:36). The nearest candidate counterexample — the backend's CLI state store — protects only the backend↔GitHub leg: github-auth.guard.ts:21-26 and cli-auth.store.ts:21-35 mint a `{stateToken, csrf}` pair with the port bound in, and auth.controller.ts:119-129 derives the redirect port from the consumed state, but the `csrf` value is never transmitted to the CLI (no occurrence of `csrf`/`state` anywhere under packages/cli/src), and `consumeCode` (cli-auth.store.ts:56-64) validates only existence and a 60s expiry, not which listener redeems the code. So a code minted for the attacker's own account is redeemable by any CLI listener. Attack: during the 30s window (login.ts:229-237), a visited page or any unprivileged local process sprays `fetch`/`img src` at `http://127.0.0.1:<candidate>/callback?code=<attacker code>`; the CLI exchanges it (login.ts:56) and persists the attacker's accessToken/refreshToken/activeWorkspace via saveSession (login.ts:138), after which victim `docs import`/`files upload` writes into the attacker's workspace. Classic OAuth login-CSRF / session fixation, in the crypto-auth lane. login.ts is the only loopback callback implementation in the repo (grep for 127.0.0.1/loopback across packages/**/src), so no guarded variant exists elsewhere. docs/design/cli.md:190-198 points at rest-api.md for "CSRF details", which describes only the backend-side state, making the gap read as covered.
